brief: Owner, 2026-09-17: find startups based in Mumbai that are currently struggling, which TVF could acquire for little to no resources or back with its support. Every lead is a startup with public evidence of trouble, confirmed to be in the Mumbai region, small enough to be cheap, ranked by how much TVF's content, audience and distribution could change its trajectory. Sector is not a filter: it is the tvf_fit criterion, so narrowing to media-only later is a weight or a gate in this file, not a new harvest.

geography.guidance: Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane, which is how Indian startup coverage uses 'Mumbai-based'. A lead is placed in Mumbai by, in order of trust: an address or a 400xxx/401xxx PIN on its own website; a headline that says 'Mumbai-based X' or 'Mumbai's X'; its news coverage placing it in Mumbai more often than anywhere else. Placed elsewhere on the same evidence, the mumbai_region gate archives it. Unplaced passes the gate (Invariant 1) but earns nothing on mumbai_confirmed, so it sinks below the review band until something places it.

rubric.label: Public evidence the startup is struggling
rubric.guidance: 1.0: a headline that the company itself shut down, laid people off, delayed salaries, went into insolvency, raised a down or rescue round, or sold in a distress sale, or its own website saying it has closed. 0.5: a softer sign -- a bridge round, sale talks, a founder exit, a pivot, closing one unit -- or the quiet version: a small round two and a half years ago, nothing since, and its website going dark. 0: checked, nothing.

rubric.label: How recent that evidence is
rubric.guidance: 1.0 within six months, 0.5 within twelve, 0 older. 'Currently struggling' is the brief; a 2024 layoff at a company that has since recovered is history.

rubric.label: Confirmed to be based in Mumbai
rubric.guidance: 1.0 when its own website carries a Mumbai-region address or PIN, or a headline says it is Mumbai-based; 0.5 when its coverage places it in Mumbai but also elsewhere; 0 when nothing places it.

rubric.label: Small enough to acquire or back for little
rubric.guidance: From the largest round its headlines state: up to $5M is 1.0, up to $20M is 0.5, beyond that 0. No stated round is not assessed; the zero-unverified rule then scores it 0 and records that nobody knows.

rubric.label: TVF's content, audience or distribution would change its trajectory
rubric.guidance: From the words its coverage and its own site use to describe it, against startup_discovery.sector_tiers: media, content, entertainment, gaming, audio, edtech, community and youth products 1.0; consumer brands and consumer apps TVF's reach helps sell 0.5; fintech, SaaS, logistics, health and other businesses TVF's audience does not move 0.

rubric.label: Something worth having: a live product, an app people use, a brand
rubric.guidance: 1.0 when its website is up or its App Store app carries at least 1,000 ratings; 0.5 when the site is gone but an app or a body of coverage remains; 0 when nothing does.

rubric.label: A founder or director we can write to
rubric.guidance: Set by the site-scrape pass (Find contacts on sites): 1.0 a named person's own address, 0.5 a role inbox, 0 nothing.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: raised an ordinary round in the last twelve months
score_modifiers.guidance: A company that closed a normal round in the last year is not out of runway, whatever else a headline says. Bridge and down rounds do not count here; they are distress.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: shut down more than a year ago
score_modifiers.guidance: A company that closed a year or more ago has usually lost its team and its users. Its brand or code may still be worth a conversation, so this lowers the score rather than ruling it out.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: no public sign of struggle
score_modifiers.guidance: Its coverage and its website were read and nothing shows struggle: no shutdown, layoffs, salary delays, down or rescue round, sale talks, pivot, and it has not gone quiet. The brief is startups that are struggling, so a healthy Mumbai startup is ranked below the review line instead of riding its fit and a small round into it. Added 2026-09-17 after the first list: 57 of 59 Mumbai-confirmed leads showed no sign of struggle. Weekly harvests keep reading its news; the day a headline shows trouble, the penalty lifts.

gates.label: Based in the Mumbai region
gates.guidance: Fires only when the evidence places the company somewhere else. Unplaced passes.

gates.label: Not a unicorn, a listed company or a big group's unit
gates.guidance: A round of $50M or more in its headlines, 'unicorn' or a listing in them, or a name in startup_discovery.major_companies. Those are not acquisitions for little to no resources.

gates.label: Not already sold
gates.guidance: A headline that another company acquired it. The sale is history, not an opportunity.

gates.label: Not long gone
gates.guidance: Fires when the newest sign of life -- a headline, a working website -- is more than three years old.

startup_discovery.guidance: Historical news-discovery configuration. New companies come only from Apollo; sector tiers, publishers and event windows remain inputs to named-company qualification.

Mumbai startup (layoffs OR "lays off" OR "shuts down" OR "shut down" OR insolvency OR "salary delays" OR "winds down")

"Mumbai-based" (D2C OR brand OR app OR platform) raises (seed OR angel OR "pre-Series A" OR "Series A")

sources.name: Apollo.io company and decision-maker search
sources.detail: tools/discover_apollo.py uses this project's saved constraints; contact roles and verified work addresses come from Apollo.

self_exclusion.guidance: Same affiliates as Segment 1 must never enter this pool either. In this segment 'tvf' is also a whole-word pattern: startup news calls TVF 'TVF', and the first dry run (2026-09-17) put it on its own acquisition list. Whole-word matching keeps names like TVFoods out of reach.

enrichment.guidance: Apollo supplies new contacts in the target roles. Existing score, geographic and site-verification restrictions and credit caps apply. Websites are read only for qualification evidence.

sender.name: SET_ME
sender.title: Corporate Development, The Viral Fever
sender.postal_address: SET_ME street address for the email footer (CAN-SPAM)
sender.guidance: Sender name and title for the shared sign-off. The address is retained as an optional footer field and omitted from the default email footer (owner, 2026-10-09). The sending address comes from the connected Gmail account.

send_window.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-12: "I want you to send mails to the sender's time region between 10 to 10:30AM and that must be randmized not like all mail going at 10:15 some must be going at 10:17 some at 10:13 and so on after approval implement it". Each approved email goes out at its own random second between start and end on its RECIPIENT's clock (10:00 in Mumbai is 05:30 in London, too early to be read), drawn when it is approved and shown in Approved as "Goes out", with the time in India beside it. Where the recipient is comes from what the lead holds -- the person's own Apollo record, the company's state or city, a phone's area code, its country -- and the reason is kept on the email (tools/send_window.py). Monday to Friday on the recipient's clock (weekdays_only): an approval after today's window, or at a weekend, takes the next weekday's. An email whose window passes unsent (the server down, its address at its daily limit) moves to the next window at a new random time, never later the same day. Never two emails from one address closer than min_gap_seconds; never one sooner than min_lead_seconds after its approval. To send on the sender's clock instead (every email 10:00-10:30 India time) set timezone_of to "sender"; to switch the window off set enabled to false -- the stored times are cleared and approvals go out as soon as they can, as before. docs/runbook.md, "Goes out". Sending is paused for this project (sending_paused). Its startups are in Mumbai and elsewhere in India, so one that names no country is taken to be Indian (assumed_country).

outreach.subject_max_words_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-13: "subject for all emails for all services should be less than 5 or equal to 5 words". Every rendered subject is checked against this (tools/draft_render.capped_subject): one over it uses its template's subject_fallback, and one still over it is not drafted, so a longer subject never ships. "Re:" in front of a follow-up is not counted.

templates.subject: A conversation worth having
templates.guidance: First touch. Deliberately ambiguous about acquisition - founders hear 'strategic' and choose how to read it. Human-approved per draft like every template. Subject (owner, 2026-10-13): "A conversation worth having", at most five words and no company name.

templates.subject: Re: {{opener_subject}}
templates.guidance: The follow-up to the corporate development note: the same voice and the same 20-minute ask.

follow_ups.guidance: Owner, 2026-10-23: "Make follo ups for all", after "set only 1 follow up after 4 days" for LCX Clipping. One follow-up, four days after the first email went out with no reply, in the same Gmail thread ("Re: <the first email's subject>"), from the same address, signed by the person whose Gmail the thread is in. It is a draft in the Follow-ups tab and needs approval like any email. Any reply stops it at once (an auto-reply lets it resume); Stop follow-ups ends the thread by hand; the database refuses one after a reply (sql/23).

outreach.guidance: Identical pipeline to Segment 1: drafted -> human-approved -> sent, one touch per company enforced by the database. The footer -- the sign-off -- is one setting for the whole segment (outreach.footer.text), edited in the app under Outreach -> Footer; templates end with {{footer}}.

footer.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-09: the sign-off, with the postal address omitted. The owner, 2026-10-13: the opt-out line is removed from every project's footer ("remove the last line from every single service"); any reply that is not neutral still stops all mail to that address. Edited in Outreach -> Footer. Postal addresses are optional; templates end with {{footer}}.

outreach.default_cc_guidance: The owner, 2026-10-22: "add a feature to cc someone from the software itself. Make default cc to the email amritanshv@lightscameraexperiment.com and obvio make a toggle to switch that off". Every email of this project is copied to these addresses unless the person approving it switches that off in the email (the CC toggle) or changes the list. The list an email is approved with is the one it goes out with (outreach.cc, sql/39, frozen at approval): changing this default never changes an email already approved. A reply from one of these addresses is not taken for the recipient's reply. [] copies nobody by default.

sourcing.guidance: Owner decision 2026-10-19: all new leads and contacts come from Apollo. Existing project constraints, gates and scoring remain. Company websites and news verify already-known leads; they do not discover new ones. Clipping is exempt.

apollo_discovery.guidance: Mumbai Metropolitan Region and TVF-relevant small businesses. Apollo results are candidates: existing named-company news/site checks must establish distress, recency, deal size and acquisition status.
